name: Node Wiring Test
author: pgianotto
description: Pick an FPP model and step or auto-chase through it one node at a time, using FPP's own channel-test API, to visually verify wiring order against what each node's position is supposed to be. Built to catch miswired/reversed/crossed pixel strings before a show runs.

privacy.summary: Lights one node at a time on a model you pick by calling FPP's own local channel-test API. Optionally, on your command only, streams a USB camera attached to this device over your local network so a phone/tablet/laptop viewing this page can see it. Nothing is sent further than that.

sends.to: devices on your local network that you point at this FPP box's IP and the camera stream's port
sends.what: live MJPEG video from a USB camera attached to this FPP device
sends.why: so a phone/tablet/laptop viewing the Node Wiring Test page can see and auto-scan a camera that's physically connected to the FPP box rather than to the viewing device

systemChanges.what: On your explicit 'Start Pi Camera' action only, starts a background process (api.php's camera/start) that runs ffmpeg against a USB camera device and serves it as MJPEG over a local HTTP port. You stop it with 'Stop Pi Camera' (or by restarting fppd); it is not installed as a system service and does not start on boot.

privacy.other: Temporarily overrides live output on the selected model's channels while a test is running/stepping, the same way FPP's built-in Channel Output Test page does. Stopping the test (or leaving the page) clears the override; nothing is written to FPP's configuration or persisted, aside from the camera stream's own PID/log files under media/plugindata while it's running.
